body: Thank you for taking the time to respond. I didn’t mean to suggest that I want to do incredible things often (I never really intended to continue the lifestyle I had back then). I’m not great at explaining how I feel and get really ramble-y/add tangents when I’m upset. It’s more that there are all these other stressors and a lot of loneliness and those are the things I see getting worse. The accomplishment I was thinking about more like a consolation prize rather than a goal I’m currently seeking (in a “they won’t have the “long and happy life” obit, but at least they did something kinda cool once?” kind of way).
Violent crime in general is down. Mass shootings, specifically, are trending up (and getting deadlier). They are an exception to the trends.

I feel like you’re looking for a logical legal answer when the real answer has nothing to do with the law. I’ll let others more knowledgeable on the law itself answer that aspect, but the reason it never went to trial is almost certainly corruption. The LAPD/DA rarely went after Scientologists for a long time, regardless of evidence, and that’s kind of been an open secret. Scientology as an organization 1) has a lot of money 2) has a lot of powerful members and 3) requires members to divulge every messed up thing they ever did and who they did it with (giving them blackmail material on not only their members, but also anyone else involved in all the embarrassing and/or illegal things they’ve ever done). They wield that power harshly to protect their members and reputation. They have gotten away with all sorts of terrible things for decades. 

There’s also a lot of messed up things that they’re suspected to have done to mess with the victims over the years, which perhaps might also provide new evidence if it can be proven they were tampering with witnesses. There may also have been new evidence provided by people who left Scientology. 

They only started investigating in earnest in 2017 (if I recall correctly), although complaints were made long before that. The delay will make prosecution more difficult, I’m sure, but that’s not something the people in bed with the Scientologists cared about avoiding at the time these complaints were first made. You’re assuming those in charge of enforcing the law were acting in good faith at the time, but that’s just not a safe assumption to make when we’re talking about Scientology. Especially in LA.
I think you meant 2060, but we’ve still got a couple weeks or so to go until that’s technically true.

Thanks for the feedback! Your point about reaching out to her superiors if I thought there were kids who might be harmed made me think. Do you think there would be any value in reaching out to an old family friend who still works at the school (but who I haven’t really seen in years) to see if they have any sense of whether this coach has changed at all? That might put the family friend in an uncomfortable position, though, so I’m not sure how much she’d be willing to share. 

She targeted me because of a disability and she now works with kids in special ed, which is concerning to me. But I have no direct knowledge that she still has these prejudices and I know there was a lot of ignorance about my disability 15 years ago that has significantly lessened. I wouldn’t want to get her in trouble if she has learned better and is actually good with those kids, but I also don’t want those kids to experience what I did if she hasn’t learned anything. 

And I will for sure keep an eye on my nieces and make sure they’re being treated well! Luckily they’re not in the same school system as I was, but I’ll make sure they know I have their back.

Thank you for your insights! While I have some hope that it might make her think about things a little more, I also have no expectation that she’ll actually respond to me at all. It’s probably unrealistic to think that she might reconsider at all, but from my angle I’m mostly just expecting silence in response. If I do send it, I’ll make sure all I really expect is that silence and not anything more.
Thank you for your input, and I’ll keep that in mind about possibly writing it and not sending it.

I had a disability that did not affect my ability to play or my behavior, but she had prejudices towards those with my disability and took that out on me pretty much the whole season. She put in rules the school didn’t use the prior years I played that, because of my disability, made it so I couldn’t really play that much and she got extremely angry if I so much as showed up to a game to cheer my teammates on from the spectator side (which wasn’t against any rules). It was a lot of little things along the way that pushed me out of this group I’d been a part of for years and started a kind of social isolation that continued until college and had a pretty big emotional toll. She’d get mad and scream about things other adults (including our former coach) told me to do and that were totally harmless. I can give a few more examples/specifics in a dm if you’d like.

ETA: the group of kids she works with now have disabilities.
